Keywords: TestClient httpx sync test pytest install httpx
Description: Use FastAPI's TestClient (wraps httpx) for synchronous endpoint tests. Requires httpx to be installed separately. Test functions are plain def — not async.
When to Use: Testing HTTP responses status codes and JSON shapes without needing async
Code Example:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_read_main():
    response = client.get('/')
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {'msg': 'Hello World'}
Fixtures: pip install httpx — required even though it is not listed as a direct FastAPI dependency
Anti-Pattern: Making test functions async def when using TestClient — async def is not needed and causes complications

Keywords: async test anyio httpx ASGITransport AsyncClient pytest mark anyio
Description: For async test functions use httpx.AsyncClient with ASGITransport — not TestClient. TestClient does not work inside async def test functions. Requires anyio and httpx.
When to Use: When your test itself must call async functions (async DB queries etc.) alongside the HTTP client
Code Example:
import pytest
from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient
from main import app

@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_root():
    async with AsyncClient(
        transport=ASGITransport(app=app),
        base_url='http://test'
    ) as ac:
        response = await ac.get('/')
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {'message': 'Tomato'}
Fixtures: pip install anyio httpx pytest-anyio — anyio provides the pytest.mark.anyio marker
Anti-Pattern: Using TestClient inside an async def test — TestClient magic breaks inside async context

Keywords: dependency override app dependency_overrides get_db test db session fake
Description: Replace the real get_db yielding dependency with a test session using app.dependency_overrides. Inject in-memory or test DB sessions without touching production data.
When to Use: Isolating route tests from the production database
Fixtures: test_db fixture creates an isolated session; clear() ensures no state leaks between tests
Anti-Pattern: Hitting the production database in tests — causes data corruption and flaky tests

Keywords: override auth get_current_user mock user bypass JWT fake user fixture
Description: Bypass authentication in tests by overriding get_current_user with a fake user object. No need to generate real JWT tokens.
When to Use: Testing protected routes without coupling tests to the auth implementation
Fixtures: Combine with db override fixture for full isolation
Anti-Pattern: Generating and verifying real JWT tokens in every test — slow and couples tests to SECRET_KEY

Keywords: parametrize mark.parametrize multiple inputs edge cases validation table-driven
Description: Use pytest.mark.parametrize to run the same test with multiple inputs. Best for testing validation boundaries and status codes across many payloads.
When to Use: Testing endpoint input validation with both valid and invalid payloads
Fixtures: Combine with client fixture from dependency overrides
Anti-Pattern: Writing one test function per edge case — duplication and poor coverage visibility

Keywords: Annotated fixture pytest conftest shared client session scope reuse
Description: Define reusable fixtures in conftest.py. Use session scope for expensive objects (DB engine). Use function scope for things that must reset per test (DB transaction).
When to Use: When multiple test modules share the same test client and DB setup
Fixtures: session scope for engine, module scope for client, function scope for DB rollbacks
Anti-Pattern: Repeating TestClient(app) setup in every test file

Keywords: background tasks BackgroundTasks mock patch assert called test
Description: Background tasks run after the response is returned. TestClient (sync) runs them synchronously inline. Use unittest.mock.patch to assert background task functions were called with the correct args.
When to Use: When a route triggers email sending or external webhooks via BackgroundTasks
Code Example:
from unittest.mock import patch

def test_register_sends_email(client):
    with patch('app.routers.users.send_welcome_email') as mock_email:
        r = client.post('/users/', json={'email': 'x@y.com', 'password': 'pw'})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    mock_email.assert_called_once_with('x@y.com')
Fixtures: TestClient runs background tasks synchronously — no need for special async handling
Anti-Pattern: Using AsyncClient for background task tests — AsyncClient does NOT execute background tasks synchronously

Keywords: lifespan context manager test startup shutdown with TestClient
Description: Use TestClient as a context manager (with statement) to trigger app lifespan startup and shutdown events during tests.
When to Use: When your app has lifespan startup logic (DB pool Redis connection ML model) that must run before tests
Code Example:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_with_lifespan():
    with TestClient(app) as client:
        # lifespan startup has run at this point
        response = client.get('/predict?x=2')
        assert response.status_code == 200
    # lifespan shutdown runs on with-block exit
Fixtures: TestClient(app) used as a context manager triggers lifespan on __enter__ and __exit__
Anti-Pattern: Creating TestClient(app) without a with-block when the app has lifespan events — startup/shutdown won't run
